51220165.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to N-terminal GST-tagged Hsp90 (unknown origin) expressed in Escherichia coli by ITC method
51220165.references_previous: 27. M. Aeluri, S. Chamakuri, B. Dasari, S. K. Guduru, R. Jimmidi, A. Jogula and P. Arya, Chem Rev, 2014, 114, 4640-4694. 31. C. Abad-Zapatero and J. T. Metz, Drug Discov. Today, 2005, 10, 464-469.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - 4.5 Isothermal t: Peptides binding capacity to Hsp90 were carried out by MicroCal iTC200 titration calorimeter (Malvern). Peptides were titrated into a solution of Hsp90 using the following conditions: Hsp90N was diluted into 30 μM with pure water and 300 μL protein buffer was inserted into the sample cell. The syringe was filled with peptides solution in the same buffer condition. 800 μM solution of peptides were titrated into the sample cell at 30 °C by two microliter aliquots. The whole procedure of the injection used 180 s intervals and a stirring speed of 1000 rpm. In addition, the first 0.5 μL of the peptides solution was titrated for prevention of initial interfering, following that 19 injections of 2.0 μL of syringe solution was titrated into 300 μL protein solution of Hsp90 constantly. Heat release caused by diluting protein into buffer was subtracted as blank values for each injection. Association constants (Ka = 1/Kd), enthalpy values (ΔH) and entropy values (ΔS) were obtained from curve-fitting according to the corrected heat values by the Origin software package. BEI value was utilized to quantify the binding capacity. BEI used both the determined binding affinity and molecular weight of a ligand for its target. 27 is an ideal BEI value of the mean value of the molecular weight of approved drugs (333 g/M) with affinity ka value of 1 nM. Thus, for the peptides, the larger BEI value is, the better peptides we obtained 31. The detailed equation of BEI value calculation is shown as follows combined with the molecular weight in kDa: BEI = (-log(Kd))/Mw
